compositionMeaning: Example composition dependencies; children and slots are explicitly supplied by the author.

authoringRules.title: Choose clear flow representations
authoringRules.description: Use labeled flowcharts, connected cards, ordered steps or other accessible visual representations for processes and relationships. Use ASCII or text-art diagrams only when the user explicitly asks for them.

authoringRules.title: Compose freely
authoringRules.description: Choose the structure, layout and visual treatment that suit your content. Combine native HTML, custom CSS and Weft as needed. The examples are starting points, not a required format.

authoringRules.title: Use Weft where it helps
authoringRules.description: Reach for existing Weft components, typography, spacing and semantic colors when they serve your purpose. Custom compositions are welcome.

authoringRules.title: Keep content readable
authoringRules.description: Maintain contrast between text and its background in light and dark themes. Use labels as well as color to communicate meaning.

authoringRules.title: Keep motion comfortable
authoringRules.description: Prefer stationary content. Respect reduced-motion preferences and avoid flashing or unnecessary movement.

authoringRules.title: Make content accessible
authoringRules.description: Use meaningful headings and links, image alternatives, table headers, keyboard access and visible focus. Keep content readable on narrow screens and when zoomed.

authoringRules.title: Confirm exceptions
authoringRules.description: Before overriding contrast, motion or basic accessibility safeguards, explain the specific exception and its impact and obtain explicit user confirmation. Confirmation applies only to that exception.
